brief: JPM's recent bullish Asian tech note argued valuations had already priced in an earnings downturn that had not materialized: the region had suffered its fourth 20%+ correction since 2022, yet roughly 80% of companies still showed positive earnings revisions, and forward P/E (ex-memory) and price-to-book had compressed toward historical averages while ROE stayed elevated. Since that report, selling has intensified, including in Taiwan, previously the last major AI market not yet in the liquidation. JPM maintains its constructive view and points to supporting data: hyperscaler datacenter capex is forecast to rise 85% in 2026 and another 70% in 2027 toward $1 trillion, public cloud revenue growth has accelerated to 50% y/y, and AI token demand is growing roughly 17x y/y. It flags one tension: Q3 capex at the four major cloud providers rose about $45bn versus only $13bn of incremental cloud revenue. Classic semiconductor cycle-peak signals (rising inventories, shortening lead times, falling compute prices) are still absent, but JPM warns the real risk is earnings expectations eventually catching down to prices.
